rationale: A string InvoiceNumber has distinct domain meaning, so model it as ConceptAs<string>.
The Guid-backed OrderId is the actual Chronicle event-source ID, so use EventSourceId<Guid>.
It is the real Chronicle stream identity, and a string-backed EventSourceId is allowed without a Guid factory.
Optional presence should be represented with a nullable concept reference, not a null wrapped value.
Enums already express a closed domain concept and should not be wrapped.
A DTO-only page-size with no domain meaning should remain primitive.
An entity ID that is not a Chronicle stream identity should be modeled as a value concept.
Changing stored shape and generation of an existing event type is an event migration concern.
A sensitive natural identifier should not be used directly as an event-source ID; use a random surrogate.
Do not place [Key], [Subject], or [PII] on an EventSourceId-derived member.
Arc authentication, claims, roles, and sign-in state are outside this concept and event-source skill.
Key rotation, erasure, retention, and redaction policy are Chronicle compliance concerns, not concept modeling.
